newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot fuel oil prices hold despite NYMEX slide.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot fuel oil prices hold despite NYMEX slide.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices held relatively steady again Wednesday despite the NYMEX crude slide, still buoyed by a firm bunker market and relatively tight prompt supplies, industry sources said.
"The bunker market is still very strong, and there's not a lot of supply coming into the market," said one cash trader.
But others said soft demand and faltering crude prompted buyers to back off, leaving the market a little toppy.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent was unchanged at about $21.25 a barrel, while November paper at $21.15-35 again lost slightly with crude, traders said.
NYH December one percent paper also was pegged slightly lower at $21.35-55.
High sulphurs in New York were still underpinned by strong bunkers, with 2.2 percent talked unchanged at about $20.
At the U.S. Gulf, prices again were stable, with one percent still at $20.00-25 and three percent at about $20.50.
Traders said 50,000 barrels of prompt USG three percent sold late Tuesday at $20.85 (FOB Miss River), while 65,000 barrels in Beaumont, Texas, were done Tuesday at $20.75.
No NYH or USG deals were reported today.
Gas prices Wednesday at the New York City gate gained almost 10 cents to the mid-$2.70s/mmBtu versus NYH one percent resid at a $3.37/mmBtu equivalent.
